To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CHK2 gene does not contribute to hereditary predisposition of breast cancer in the Finnish population, at least not as a major susceptibility gene.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CHK2 mutations are not a significant cause of hereditary breast cancer in the Finnish population, but that this may not be true in other populations.
the role of CHK2 in hereditary predisposition of breast cancer is unclear and needs to be studied in other populations as well.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CHK2 does contribute significantly to breast cancer susceptibility, but the contribution is very minor.
CHK2 does contribute to hereditary predisposition of breast cancer, but only in families with a strong family history and a high penetrance of cancer.

CHK2 is not a major breast cancer predisposition gene in the Finnish population, but the possibility that CHK2 may contribute to the risk of breast cancer in a small number of cases can not be excluded.
